title: Aluminum Wiring Instead of Copper
description: For building wire, aluminum is the classic copper substitute: it conducts about 61% as well as copper by volume but is far lighter and cheaper per ampere carried. Utilities have run aluminum distribution lines for decades. Terminations need anti-oxidant paste and proper lugs — the trade is workmanship for cost.
tradeoff: Aluminum needs a larger gauge for the same current and careful termination; copper is more forgiving and compact.

title: Sodium-Ion Batteries Instead of Lithium-Ion
description: Sodium is a thousand times more abundant than lithium and mined from seawater and salt flats. Sodium-ion cells trade some energy density for dramatically cheaper, geopolitically calmer raw materials — ideal for stationary storage and low-cost vehicles.
tradeoff: Lower energy density means bigger, heavier packs; best where weight matters less than cost.

title: Ferrite Magnets Instead of Neodymium
description: Where maximum strength is not needed, cheap ferrite (ceramic) magnets replace rare-earth neodymium: no mining of rare earths, a fraction of the price, and excellent corrosion resistance. Motors get bigger; the planet gets a break.
tradeoff: Weaker field means larger magnets and motors for the same torque.

title: GFRP Rebar Instead of Steel Rebar
t: GFRP Rebar Instead of Steel Rebar

tradeoff: Must be pre-bent at the factory; design codes are newer and stricter.

title: Fly-Ash Concrete Instead of Pure Portland Cement
t: Fly-Ash Concrete Instead of Pure Portland Cement

tradeoff: Slower set times need schedule planning; supply of quality fly ash varies by region.

tradeoff: Limited to alkaline environments; platinum still rules acidic PEM cells.

title: Hempcrete Instead of Concrete Block

tradeoff: Requires a structural frame; drying time is long and labor is specialized.

title: OSB Instead of Plywood
description: Oriented strand board presses fast-growing wood strands into structural panels at lower cost than plywood veneers. For sheathing and subfloors it performs comparably; it swells more if soaked and holds screws slightly less well.
tradeoff: Keep it dry during construction; choose plywood where edges stay exposed.
